robot.name: K-Scale K-Bot
robot.status_notes: Pre-orders canceled and refunded in November 2025; company laid off most staff and open-sourced hardware (CERN-OHL-S-2.0) and software (MIT). Operations appear to be ceasing as of Humanoids Daily report.
intended_use_cases: household chores (mopping floors, preparing bread in toasters)
research and development platform for humanoid robotics

height.notes: Source says 1.4m tall (approximately 4.7 inches); 1.4 m is about 55 inches, so the 4.7 inches figure appears to be a typo. We use 1.4 m as the value.

battery.notes: Battery capacity not specified; source only lists battery life of 4 hours.

walking_speed.notes: No walking speed found in sources.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: No total DoF figure found in sources.

hands.description: Swappable end effectors; hands are easily swappable using a camera lens style mount (company engineer comment on Hacker News).

compute.description: Modular sensor and compute suite that is upgradable; no specific processor or model named.

actuators.description: Third-party video title indicates Quasi Direct Drive (QDD) Robstride actuators, but no transcript was reviewed.

availability.notes: Starting price reported as $10,999 by Interesting Engineering before pre-orders were canceled and refunded in November 2025. The shop URL was shared by the founder on Hacker News; availability is now closed.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: K-Bot is described with adaptable end effectors for different tasks; a company engineer on Hacker News says hands are easily swappable using a camera lens style mount. No dexterity demo or success rates were found.
caveats: No dexterity demonstration or manipulation task evidence.
Swappable hands are a hardware design claim, not a proven manipulation capability.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Initial release was expected to have basic locomotion, balance control, voice commands, and app-based control using pre-defined command sets; full autonomy was projected for June 2028 with less than 1 human intervention per day. A low-latency teleoperation demo was reported, which is explicitly teleoperated, not autonomous.
caveats: Autonomy projections are future company claims, not demonstrated capabilities.
The only reported demo was teleoperated, so no autonomous task execution was observed.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: The robot was expected to have basic locomotion and balance control at initial release. No walking speed, fall rate, or whole-body control demo was found.
caveats: Only a future capability claim; no observed locomotion or balance video with transcript/review.
No mobility metrics found.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: The robot is equipped with RGB camera, stereo vision, ultra-wide FOV camera, far-field microphones, and stereo speakers. No perception benchmark or scene understanding demo was found.
caveats: Sensors are listed but no perception task or accuracy data was provided.
No autonomous scene understanding demonstration.

human_interaction.summary: Initial release expected voice commands and app-based control using pre-defined command sets. The robot includes far-field microphones and stereo speakers.
caveats: Voice commands were a planned feature, not demonstrated in reviewed sources.
No interaction reliability or user study evidence.

endurance_reliability.summary: Battery life is listed as 4 hours. No operating hours, failure rates, or reliability metrics were found.
caveats: Battery life is a spec, not observed runtime.
No reliability testing or field data was disclosed.

human_environment_fit.summary: The robot is 1.4 m tall and 34 kg with a 10 kg payload, intended for household chores like mopping and preparing bread in toasters. No safety certification or home deployment evidence was found.
caveats: No safety testing or human-proximity certification disclosed.
Discontinued before widespread home use.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Humanoids Daily reported that K-Scale had recently begun shipping its first K-Bot Founder's Edition units and that pre-orders were later canceled. No customer names, unit counts, or output metrics were provided.
caveats: Only media report, not customer confirmation.
Small number of units shipped, no named customer or operational data.
Pre-orders were canceled, so no ongoing commercial deployment.

accessibility_value.summary: The K-Bot was positioned as an open-source personal robot with a starting price of $10,999. The RL library and sim2real pipeline were released to developers. After shutdown, hardware was released under CERN-OHL-S-2.0 and software under MIT.
caveats: Robot is no longer for sale; pre-orders refunded.
Open-source release is a company action, but no active support or community adoption verified.
Price reported by media, not official spec page.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: K-Bot was an open-source humanoid prototype from K-Scale Labs (Palo Alto) that gained attention for a low reported starting price ($10,999) and open-source development stack. The company shipped a small number of Founder's Edition units and demonstrated low-latency teleoperation, but canceled all pre-orders and open-sourced its IP in November 2025 after failing to raise funding. No autonomous operation, DoF, walking speed, or independent benchmarks were found.
strongest_positive_evidence: Open-source RL library and sim2real pipeline released to developers (source 003).
Modular compute and swappable end effectors (source 001).
Hardware released under CERN-OHL-S-2.0 and software under MIT after shutdown (source 002).
Low price point for a humanoid, even if ultimately not available (source 001).
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No independent benchmark, autonomy demo, or reliability data.
No total DoF, hand DoF, battery capacity, walking speed, or compute model.
Only a media report of Founder's Edition shipping; no customer names or unit counts.
Teleoperation demo is the only reported demo; no autonomous task execution.
conflicting_claims: Height: 1.4 m tall (about 55 inches) vs 'approximately 4.7 inches' in source, likely a typo.
Price: $10,999 (Interesting Engineering) vs $8,999 in YouTube title (source 11, not reviewed).
Shutdown status: Humanoids Daily says operations appear to be ceasing, but a social media reply claims it hasn't shut down (source 2 mentions conflicting reports).
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit any autonomous task execution; only teleoperation was reported.
Do not treat the 2028 full autonomy projection as current capability.
Do not infer specs from video titles without transcript.
Do not describe K-Bot as commercially available or deployed at scale.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: K-Scale K-Bot was an open-source humanoid robot from K-Scale Labs (Palo Alto) with reported specs of 1.4 m height, 34 kg weight, 10 kg payload, 4-hour battery life, modular compute, swappable end effectors, and a starting price of $10,999. It targeted developers with an open-source RL library and sim2real pipeline. The company shipped a small number of Founder's Edition units and demonstrated low-latency teleoperation, but canceled all pre-orders and refunded deposits in November 2025 after failing to raise funding, then open-sourced hardware (CERN-OHL-S-2.0) and software (MIT). No autonomous operation, DoF, walking speed, or independent benchmarks were found.
strongest_evidence: Open-source RL library and sim2real pipeline released (source 003).
Modular compute and swappable end effectors (source 001).
IP released under CERN-OHL-S-2.0 and MIT after shutdown (source 002).
weakest_evidence: No independent benchmark, intervention log, or failure rate.
No DoF, battery capacity, walking speed, or compute model.
Only a media report of Founder's Edition shipping; no customer names or unit counts.
Teleoperation is the only reported demo; no autonomous task execution.
known_do_not_credit: Autonomous task execution; only teleoperation was reported.
Full autonomy by June 2028 as current capability.
Open-source IP as proof of commercial availability.
Any video content beyond titles in sources 6-11.
